name: kornia
description: 🐍 Geometric Computer Vision Library for Spatial AI
one_liner: A toolbox of image-processing and 3D-geometry building blocks for people writing computer-vision software, built to run fast on graphics cards.
buyer: A computer-vision engineer at a startup building AR, robotics, or document-scanning software who doesn't want to rewrite geometry math from scratch.
business_use_cases: A robotics startup uses its camera-calibration and depth tools to get a robot's vision stack working faster.
A document-scanning app uses its perspective-warp and feature-matching tools to straighten and stitch photographed pages.
An AR startup uses its differentiable geometry to align virtual objects with a phone camera feed in real time.

money_ideas.idea: Paid consulting and support contracts for companies shipping it inside production computer-vision products.

steal_this: This is plumbing, not a product — the realistic weekend win is building one specific vertical tool on top of it (e.g. a 'scan and straighten receipts' app) rather than trying to sell the library itself.
